subject.title: feat: per-job elevated exec scoping for cron and heartbeat

question: Should OpenClaw solve #41484 as a narrow per-job/heartbeat elevated flag, or fold it into the broader non-forgeable scheduling provenance design?
rationale: The choice changes the trust boundary for elevated host exec across persisted cron jobs, agent-created schedules, heartbeat files/config, and upgrade behavior, which requires maintainer security intent.

options.title: Fold Into Scheduling Provenance
options.body: Treat #41484 as the elevated-exec requirement for the broader scheduling provenance design while explicitly keeping heartbeat modifier provenance in scope.

options.title: Implement Narrow Elevated Markers
options.body: Add per-job and heartbeat-modifier elevated approval state now, with migration and tests for create, update, and execution-time checks.

options.title: Remove Internal-Source Elevation
options.body: Fail closed for `cron-event` and `heartbeat` elevated access unless maintainers intentionally preserve a compatibility path.

recommendation.title: Fold Into Scheduling Provenance
recommendation.body: Treat #41484 as the elevated-exec requirement for the broader scheduling provenance design while explicitly keeping heartbeat modifier provenance in scope.

likelyOwner.reason: The newest cron provenance/schema work merged through #100480, making this the closest current owner path for the product/security decision.
